correctness.rationale: The exact killed-Brownian renewal survival transform gives closed first and second passage moments and the identity CV²−1=[e^(−t)/(1−e^(−t))](2−H_q(t)), with positive prefactor. For 0<q≤1, H_q increases strictly. For q≥1, a closed logarithmic second derivative and the inequality 2sinh(t/2)>t show strict log-concavity; the unique maximum decreases strictly in q>1, with endpoints above/below level 2. This yields all four cases and exactly one tangency threshold. The separate generator check establishes the two moments as bounded solutions of the correct backward Dirichlet problem, and differentiation of the original Laplace transform agrees for 48 parameter pairs. Numerics establish decimal values only, not infinite-domain uniqueness.

originality.rationale: The known generalized survival transform, second-moment framework, and CV=1 at mean-optimal renewal restart are not claimed as new. The claimed additional content is a globally exhaustive number-of-crossings classification for mismatched deterministic initial/reset distances, a strict log-concavity theorem for its exact sign function, and a unique dimensionless critical ratio. Full relevant texts and actual published-finding corpus searches were compared by model assumptions, observables and implication, without finding a stated equivalent; this is not independent certification of priority.
residual_risks: General renewal and Feynman–Kac formulas do imply exact moments by differentiation; another unindexed paper may already have established the additional shape theorem in an equivalent formulation.
Published textual and semantic searches do not prove mathematical novelty or certified first publication.
The earlier 2022 first-passage functional study was checked through its directly relevant sections and conclusion; sections concerning other functionals were not exhaustively compared line-by-line.

value.rationale: The normalized dispersion CV² is a natural reliability observable for first-passage search. The theorem gives a complete and sharp phase boundary in the physical ratio b/a: resetting slightly farther away produces a previously hidden interval of less-than-exponential passage-time fluctuations bounded by two distinct rates, while resetting sufficiently farther eliminates this interval entirely. It resolves the all-rate behavior without an arbitrary parameter slice and distinguishes nonrenewal first-excursion mismatch from standard renewal restart.
